messages.subject: [amelia] convergence issue
messages.body_plain:
I am getting the following error when trying to run Amelia:



1 Error in eigen(thetanew[2:nrow(thetanew), 2:ncol(thetanew)],

only.values = TRUE,  :infinite or missing values in 'x'


I've read through the list and have tried the fixes that have been 
suggested.  I removed about 15 cases when participants had less than 10% 
available data.  I've also tried lowering the tolerance.  I am assuming 
that at this point I should think about variables to remove.  My data 
consists of 89 questions for an epistemological beliefs scale I am 
trying to create.  Are there any suggestions as to how I should go about 
choosing questions to remove?  I've checked the correlations and there 
seems to be no multicollinearity. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated!




Laura

messages.subject: [amelia] problem with missmaps
messages.body_plain:
Antonio,
Instead of:
> missmap(k1,csvar=k1[,3],tsvar=k1[,2])
See if:
> missmap(k1,csvar=3,tsvar=2)
works in your dataset.  That is, the arguments are the column positions, not
the actual extracted columns from the matrix.  Or if this were a data frame you
could use variable names, such as:
> missmap(k1,csvar="countryname",tsvar="year")
if those names were appropriate (that is, contained in "names(k1)")

Hope all is well with you,
James

messages.subject: [amelia] problem with missmaps
messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,

Unfortunately, you need to include the time and cross-sectional
variables in the data passed to missmap and they will be mapped along
with any other variables. The missmap function relies on the image()
function at its core, so you could try to look at the source and hack
together a map that suits your needs.

If you want to draw the map without any time/cross-section
information, you can force R to treat the column as a one-column
matrix:

missmap(k1[ ,1, drop = FALSE])

Hope that helps,
matt.

Thanks for your reply. I got it now.

I was just wondering about some of the common "problems" with these maps:
often in time-serious cross-sectional data we have so many counties that we
can't really plot all their names; and if we wanna arrange country in terms
of, say, income per capita income, to see the correlation of missing data
and this indicator, than is even more difficult. I saw that you did some
tricks in this post,like plotting over country names over both sides of the
y-axis  but I can't see the code. Perhaps you and others might wanna share
some of this tricks.

http://www.iq.harvard.edu/blog/sss/archives/2009/02/missingness_map.shtml


Congratulation for your software!

Best,

Antonio.

messages.subject: [amelia] problem with missmaps
messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,

Thanks for these suggestions. The next time we update the missmap
function, we will definitely keep these in mind. You can reorder the
map currently by reordering the matrix or data frame you pass to it.
So, for income you could do:

missmap(data[order(data$income),])

Cheers,
matt.
